# GMAA

> GMAA (Governed Multi-Agent Architecture) is a governance layer for multi-agent systems. The unit of authorization is the set, not the change: an accountable human ratifies the complete set of pending changes against a system's invariants, before any of them commits.

GMAA is an open standard. The specification is licensed CC BY 4.0. The engine that implements it is source-available under PolyForm Shield 1.0.0. Author: Israel Heskiel. Canonical: gmaa.ai. Cite by version.

## Core documents
- [The specification, v1.5](https://gmaa.ai/canon.html): The buildable architecture. Coherence boundaries, single writers, the governed seat, subagent roles, the ratification flow, and the per-project instantiation checklist.
- [The thesis, The Coherence Boundary](https://gmaa.ai/thesis.html): Why the unit of authorization is the set and not only the change, why no shipping system fills that seat, and why the human in it cannot be automated away.
- [Overview](https://gmaa.ai/): What GMAA is, the gap it fills, and the line between what is claimed and what is left open.

## What is claimed, and what is not
- Established: the unit is the set, and no shipping system places an accountable human at that unit before commit.
- Open, on purpose: whether a given implementation catches every joint incoherence is earned by an adversarial test, not asserted.
